back: Benzene + Cl₂ with AlCl₃ (or Fe), room temperature, dry: electrophilic substitution.

front: Chlorination of methylbenzene in the ring

back: Cl lone pair delocalised into the ring: partial double-bond C–Cl (stronger); π cloud repels nucleophiles.
Strong C–F bonds: inert, non-flammable, low toxicity (refrigerants, propellants, anaesthetics, PTFE).
CCl₂F₂ → CClF₂• + Cl• (UV breaks the weaker C–Cl bond).
Cl• + O₃ → ClO• + O₂; ClO• + O → Cl• + O₂ (overall O₃ + O → 2O₂).

front: Why a little CFC does great damage
back: Cl• is regenerated (a catalyst), so one radical destroys many thousands of O₃ molecules.
HCFCs (broken down lower, still some harm) and HFCs (no Cl, no ozone depletion, but often greenhouse gases).
International agreement (1987) to phase out CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances.
